metadata.title: HAMSTAD WP2 Benchmark 2: isothermal moisture redistribution in a homogeneous wall (analytical case)

authors: HAMSTAD WP2 group (CTH, TNO, KUL, TUD, Technion)
source.journal: HAMSTAD WP2 Final report R-02:8, Chalmers University of Technology (EU GRD1-1999-20007)

metadata.validation_method: analytical series solution (this benchmark's published reference case)
metadata.validation_target: Moisture content profiles w(x) at t = 100, 300, 1000 h (w in kg/m3, x in m, 21 positions)
metadata.notes: Solved in the paper's OWN linear moisture-content (w) formulation: constant D_w=6.0e-10 m2/s, constant delta_p=1e-15 s -> the governing PDE in w is linear, so the humidity field is used as a pure relabel of w (capacity=1, alpha=1 in bazant_najjar gives constant D0). Isotherm nonlinearity does NOT enter this formulation: w_e=w(0.45)=19.536 and w_i=w(0.65)=30.506 kg/m3 enter only as Robin reference values. Robin coefficients beta_w = beta_p*p_sat/xi are isotherm-slope dependent but Bi~1e7 makes them quasi-Dirichlet (sensitivity <0.01 kg/m3 per 10% beta change). Tangent slopes xi_e=4.113e4 (ext), xi_i=7.433e3 (int) used; secant xi=131 would shift boundaries by ~1 kg/m3 - within the HAMSTAD acceptance band (worst participant error 2.24 kg/m3). Reference CSVs are the computed analytical solution (asymmetric Robin-Robin series), cross-checked against a published independent implementation: w(0,1000h)=19.54, w(0.20,1000h)=30.51 - exact match. RISKY-CHECK: bazant_najjar with capacity=1 must accept the parameter set as linear diffusion; if the backend enforces hc in (0,1) only as a bound, hc=0.5 is inert at alpha=1.

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: 200 mm wall thickness (Sec. 3.2 'Dimensions'). ASSUMED: 0.02 m transverse height - 1D model, no transverse physics; matches element_size so probes sit mid-strip.

physical_groups.name: face_exterior
physical_groups._comment: x=0, EXTERIOR side (small x per paper convention, Sec. 3.2 output spec)

physical_groups.name: probe_x000
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: output position x=0.00 m (exterior surface)

physical_groups.name: probe_x200
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: output position x=0.20 m (interior surface)

mesh._comment: 0.002 m elements -> 100 elements across 0.2 m: probes land exactly on nodes (0.01 m output grid), and the steep boundary layers at early times (penetration sqrt(Dw*t) = 0.5 mm at 100 h) are resolved. Field is linear in h -> quad/triangle irrelevant.

dependent_variable.name: humidity
dependent_variable._comment: h carries the MOISTURE CONTENT w [kg/m3] directly (relabel). All queries map h -> w by identity.

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: w0 = 84.7687 kg/m3 (= w(0.95) on the isotherm w=116*(1-ln(phi)/0.118)^-0.869, verified to 4 decimals), T=20 C isothermal.

boundary_conditions._comment: EXTERIOR (x=0): Robin in w-form -Dw dw/dn = beta_w (w - w_e). xi(0.45) = dw/dphi = 41.162 kg/m3 -> beta_w = beta_p*p_sat/xi = 1e-3*2339/41.162 = 5.6824e-2 m/s. u_ref = w_e = w(0.45) = 19.5356 kg/m3 (PAPER_VALUE via the isotherm). Bi = 1.9e7 -> quasi-Dirichlet; a 10% error in beta moves results by <0.01 kg/m3. beta_p = 1.0e-3 s/m and p_sat(20 C) = 2339 Pa are both PAPER_VALUEs (p.21).
INTERIOR (x=0.2): same construction. xi(0.65) = 74.317 kg/m3 -> beta_w = 1e-3*2339/74.317 = 3.1473e-2 m/s; u_ref = w_i = w(0.65) = 30.506 kg/m3.

time_stepping._comment_t_end: PAPER_VALUE: 1000 h simulation time (Sec. 3.2 output spec)
time_stepping._comment_dt: log grid 300 s -> 5e4 s sums to 1000.1 h; fine steps resolve the instant RH step at t=0 (boundary layer sqrt(Dw*t) = 0.05 mm at 1 h; 0.5 mm at 100 h)

reference_curves.label: Analytical w(x), t=100 h
reference_curves._comment:
Robin-Robin series solution of the paper's w-formulation (500 modes), ONE FILE with one column per requested time -- the paper (Output spec, p.21) asks for w(x) at 100, 300 AND 1000 h, so all three are wired.
VERIFIED against the paper's own Figures 3.2.1-3.2.4 (read at gridline crossings; the figures are raster, so no vector extraction is possible): 100 h x=2/3 cm -> 62.5/75.0 vs 62.8554/75.0545; 1000 h x=3 cm -> 42.0 vs 41.9918; 1000 h x=18/19 cm -> 43.2/37.0 vs 43.1306/36.9083. The interior half matches too, which the old spot-check never covered.
The former 'an_timeseries' entry pointed at reference/analytical_timeseries.csv, which DOES NOT EXIST -- it silently produced a reference-free plot. Removed.

queries.label: w at x=0.00 m [kg/m3]
queries._comment: identity map h->w; expect 19.54 kg/m3 from the first resolved step (quasi-Dirichlet)

queries.label: w at x=0.10 m [kg/m3]
queries._comment: primary validation quantity: 84.77 (100 h) -> 84.11 (300 h) -> 69.46 (1000 h) kg/m3

queries.label: w(x) at t=100 h [kg/m3]
queries._comment: at_time evaluates the profile ONCE, on the step crossing that instant. Without it a line_profile runs every step and a plot can only show the last one -- which is why only 1000 h used to be comparable. 2D coordinates: the backend rejects 3 on a 2D mesh.

plots.name: moisture_history_midplane
plots.title: Moisture content at x=0.10 m
plots._comment: No reference curve: the paper's requested output is w(x) profiles, not a time series, and no analytical time series file exists. The profile plots below carry the validation.

plots.name: moisture_profile_100h
plots.title: HAMSTAD BM2 - moisture content profile at t=100 h
plots._comment:
A line_profile is a SPATIAL result and must be read with source:'query' + query_key. It used to be declared source:'simulation' with x=t_hours, y=w_profile, which silently rendered NO FEM curve at all -- the plot showed only the analytical line.
The analytical solution is drawn as MARKERS, not a line: the agreement is so close that a dashed reference line sat entirely underneath the FEM curve and was invisible. 21 points is exactly the paper's requested output grid.

reference_deviation._comment: Disabled: reference_deviation pairs a TIME SERIES against a reference, and this benchmark's only reference is w(x) profiles. It used to name 'an_timeseries', whose file does not exist.
